content.title: Mark Few Show: Coach Few unpacks Gonzaga's 3-seed, Kennesaw St. matchup, NCAA Tournament streak
content.text: SPOKANE, Wash. — Gonzaga is headed back to the NCAA Tournament for the 27th consecutive time — well, 28th if you ask Mark Few and count the 2020 tournament when GU was slated to be the No. 1 overall seed before it was canceled.Regardless, the Bulldogs earned a No. 3 seed in the NCAA Tournament and will play No. 14 seed Kennesaw State on Thursday at 7 p.m. in Portland, extending one of the most remarkable streaks in college basketball.Top Videos For head coach Mark Few, the moment never gets old.“I never, ever, ever take this for granted,” Few said on the Mark Few Show after Selection Sunday. “This is one of those days where it's just great to be a college basketball coach. I think it's the greatest sporting event in the world. To see your name pop up there — never take it for granted.”Despite injuries and a challenging nonconference schedule, the Bulldogs still finished with 30 wins, just three losses, and a No. 3 seed, something Few credited to the resilience of his team.“With everything that we've been through, this a heck of an accomplishment by the guys,” Few said.First up, a Kennesaw State Owls team that won three games in three days to win the Conference USA Tournament, and brings a dangerous offensive style into the first-round matchup.“They're going to play fast. They're going to find threes. They're going to offensive rebound. They're going to apply pressure-defense,” Few said. “We have to be at our best on Thursday. We're going to have to play really, really, really well to move on past Kennesaw.”The Owls rely heavily on the three-point shot, with more than 43% of their attempts coming from beyond the arc, meaning Gonzaga must be ready for a high-scoring, up-tempo game.Few said the Zags will lean on their staff this week as preparation begins immediately with a quick turnaround before Thursday’s tip.“The staff is great. This is where you lean into your staff really, really hard,” Few said. “Everybody needs to focus on Kennesaw, but part of your staff will be focusing on BYU and (NC State and Texas).”Gonzaga enters the tournament after winning both the WCC regular-season and WCC tournament titles, but three WCC teams ultimately earned bids into the field, with Santa Clara and Saint Mary's.The Bulldogs also saw key contributions recently from freshmen Mario Saint-Supery and Davis Fogle during the conference tournament run, something Few said was critical during the comeback win over Santa Clara.“They really stepped up right when we needed it,” Few said.Gonzaga will also monitor the health of forward Jalen Warley, who returned from a thigh contusion and is still working back toward full strength.“I think he's moving better,” Few said. “I don't think he's to 100%, but he's definitely moving better, feeling better, and getting more confidence.”The Bulldogs will now prepare for their opening-round matchup just a few hours south of Spokane, a short trip Few said should help the team settle in quickly.“We'll have a couple good days of practice here, and then we got the blessing of a short travel,” Few said.Tipoff between Gonzaga and Kennesaw State is scheduled for 7 p.m. Thursday in Portland. SWX will be with the Zags in Portland all tournament long and will have the latest on SWXLocalSports.com and NonStop Local KHQ.
